title: A locally free completed coefficient line is derived complete
statement:
Let L be any rank-one locally free module over the actual completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] of a scheme S. For every compatible finite-field datum, L[0] satisfies IsDerivedComplete [def-weil-derived-complete] with its actual augmentation. This concerns arbitrary completed coefficient lines and requires no root tower or finite local models.

theorem completedLine_complete (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (WeilConjectures.completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E S))
    (hL : L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1)
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (hl : l ≠ D.p) :
    letI := WeilConjectures.integralCoefficientAbLocallyBijective.{u, u} S
    WeilConjectures.IsDerivedComplete.{d, u, u} l E S D hl
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L)

source.place: Coefficient-twist blueprint proof step 11 via perfect duality; Bhatt--Scholze Sections 3.4 and 6.5; Stacks Tag 08JJ.

proof.text: The line has a locally strictly perfect single complex: on a rank-one trivializing cover take the regular module in degree zero, with its Fin 1 product splitting, and zero terms with their Fin 0 splittings. Perfect duality identifies its derived single with its double dual. The existing constant coefficient theorem supplies completeness of the regular coefficient object. The existing ambient internal-Hom completeness theorem supplies completeness of the double dual. Naturality of quotient transitions and actual units transports its Roos triangle along the bidual isomorphism. The proved intrinsic/legacy comparison gives the exact finite-field completeness predicate.
